spillNote: the graph needs about as much memory as the finished index; this box has 31.7 GiB total and about 11.8 GiB free with the walk and Postgres running, so a 7.65M-row build spills whatever session maintenance_work_mem is set to.

2GB.method: EXTRAPOLATION — below the lowest measured resident fraction (0.195). Weakest number here.

4GB.method: interpolation between the two measured points

8GB.method: interpolation between the two measured points

16GB.method: interpolation between the two measured points

interpolationCaveat: The rows/s between the two measured points is INTERPOLATED LINEARLY IN RESIDENT FRACTION and is NOT measured. Two points cannot establish the shape of that curve, and pgvector spills in a two-pass form whose cost is not obviously linear. Treat every interpolatedUNVERIFIED number as a guess with a stated method, not as a measurement. The 1M-row @ 2GB probe in section 8 is exactly the experiment that would turn the nearest one into evidence. Note also that at 7.65M rows a 2GB setting is only 10.3% resident, which is BELOW the 19.5% of the lowest measured build — so the 2GB row is an extrapolation off the end of the data, not an interpolation inside it.
